results.summary: Keep this as Skookum's north ridge (5.4), the only documented climb here, and rewrite the name, grade, rope and descent fields that described a Class 3-4 scramble no source records.
results.evidence: Three independent accounts describe the same line: from the Green Creek side parties climb over Jaws' Tooth, rappel about 15 m (a 30 m rope just reaches) or downclimb low fifth class to the notch, then follow Skookum's north (north-east) ridge on solid, very exposed olivine at about 5.4 / low fifth class; a route database lists it as low-fifth ridge climbing after the Jaws' Tooth rappel, and a 2019 party logged it as the NE Ridge of Skookum. Both accounts that describe getting off Skookum go down the loose south-west side by third-class gullies toward the basin under Hayden, not back along the ridge (which would mean re-climbing Jaws' Tooth). No source describes a Class 3-4 route up Skookum; the row's beta, face, rock_grade and pro_needs already described the north ridge, while the name, discipline, grade, rope fields, descent and itinerary described a scramble. Round-trip time, mileage and gain were left alone (only whole-circuit figures exist). The 'stay left/west of the crest' advice was replaced: the documented line stays on the crest.

ops.expect: This is a big single-day outing, not a backpack: parties hike the Elbow Lake Trail, ford the Middle Fork Nooksack and follow the blazed Green Creek climbers' path into the Green Creek Cirque, then scramble loose third and fourth class ground out of the cirque onto the ridge where the terrain turns to famously grippy olivine/dunite rock. The ridge itself is mostly 2nd-3rd class if you stay left/west of the crest, with short 3rd-4th class steps and real exposure near the top; route-finding (staying left, not straying right onto harder terrain) is the crux of the day as much as the climbing.
ops.value: This is a big single-day outing, not a backpack: parties hike the Elbow Lake Trail, ford the Middle Fork Nooksack and follow the blazed Green Creek climbers' path into the Green Creek Cirque, then scramble loose third and fourth class ground out of the cirque onto the ridge where the terrain turns to famously grippy olivine/dunite rock. Skookum's north ridge is reached by going over Jaws' Tooth and rappelling (or downclimbing low fifth class) to the notch on its south side; from there the line stays true to the crest on solid, very exposed rock at about 5.4. The way down is the loose south-west side by third-class gullies, not back along the ridge.

Those three were changed; distance, gain and loss figures were left as the earlier audit settled them.

results.summary: Rename this to 'Standard Route (Northeast summit via South Gully and East Ridge)': every section of the page already describes that line from Lake Constance, and Crystal Pass is only the longer alternative way in.
results.evidence: A detailed 2004 account climbs Inner Constance from Lake Constance up Avalanche Canyon, the south-east couloir, the moated South Defile and South Gully to a notch on the East Ridge, then a Class 2-3 scramble to the top, and descends the same way; a December 2025 ascent log likewise approaches by the Lake Constance trail and Avalanche Canyon. No source ties Crystal Pass to the standard Inner Constance line; it appears with Mount Constance's West Arete. The row's face, beta, approach, climbing_route, pitch_detail, descent and first approach variant already describe the South Gully-East Ridge line, and the Crystal Pass way is kept as the second approach variant, so only the name changes. Not changed (still single-source, recorded earlier as open): the 'Class 4 / low 5th' grade, rock_grade 5.0 and the chimney/roof wording in hazards, pro_needs and watch_out, which the one detailed account of this line does not mention.

results.summary: Keep this row: the Wilson Glacier Headwall is a real (rarely repeated) Mount Adams route, but take out the description of the unrelated Mount Rainier 'Wilson Headwall' that had been copied into its rope and rack notes.
results.evidence: The route exists on Adams: a general reference names the Wilson Glacier Headwall among the dangerous routes up Roosevelt Cliff on the east side, and a first-hand account of the first ascent (Ed Cooper and Mike Swayne, 30 June 1961) describes traversing from Killen Creek to the Wilson Glacier, climbing north of the rock rib that splits the glacier, crossing the bergschrund, climbing the rightmost of three chimneys through the cliff band on rotten ice, verglas and rock with rockfall, then the upper Wilson Glacier, and descending the North Ridge. The rope_note sentence about '30-50 degree slopes staying left of a central rock buttress' with fifth-class rock bands near the top matches, nearly word for word, the Mount Rainier Wilson Headwall description (Wapowety Cleaver), so it and the matching rack/sling_rack items were rewritten. Not changed (only the single 1961 account speaks to them): the approach side (the first ascent came from the north, the row from Cold Springs), the grade, and the descent wording that offers both the North Ridge and the South Climb.

results.summary: This is the right Goat Mountain (the one off the Hannegan Pass Road near Mount Baker); lower its grade from Class 2-3 to Class 2, which two route descriptions give for the East Peak, and bring the few other 'Class 2-3' mentions into line.
results.evidence: Both pages were read in full this time. A detailed East Peak route description rates it 'steep heather scrambling with mild exposure (Class 2)', hands used only for balance, with a short straightforward gully near the top. A long-standing peak description (read from an archived copy) gives the East Peak as 'Difficulty: Class 2', an easy Class 2 gully that narrows and becomes exposed near the summit, and says the East Peak is not technically difficult, the real difficulty being steep, slippery heather that calls for an axe or poles. The same page sets the peak off the Mount Baker Highway / Hannegan Pass Road (FS 32), matching this row's trailhead, so it is the Goat Mountain near Mount Baker. rock_grade and the waypoint notes already said Class 2. The steep-snow pitch in pitch_detail (graded as snow) and the exposure warnings were kept; no other fields changed.
